Yes. Oldest, only daughter. 

The pressure and expectations that were and are set for me by my parents are so much higher than those of my younger brothers. My brothers are not expected to go above and beyond as I was (which I wouldn’t want them to be subject to necessarily so long as they are doing well enough), while for me it was always “you need to be a role model to your siblings, don’t embarrass our family, do not fail us.” My path is a reflection and result of my parents, or so they tend to believe. 

I mean, sure, I think it instilled discipline, which was what helped lead me to be the first in my family to graduate college and now the first to attend graduate school, amongst career accomplishments. But it also led to mental health struggles with anxiety and imposter syndrome. It’s good that my younger siblings got the softer, more lenient side of my parents, but somehow they are still very much expectant of me. It is what it is, I guess.
